findings.title: Production checker concurrency has no effective guard
findings.detail: crates/blit-core/tests/local_session.rs:1600 claims to guard end-to-end checker plumbing, but replacing Some(&local.checker_pool) with None at crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:4983 left the test green. Its converged phase has identical sequential and parallel outcomes; its changed phase lets the default run repair both files, then expects the 1- and 16-checker runs to copy zero. The pool unit test did go red when the pool itself was forced to one worker and green after exact-byte restoration, but it cannot detect production wiring removal, so the load-bearing feature can disappear while all added tests pass.

findings.title: The diagnostic checker pin is silently ignored on remote routes
findings.detail: TransferArgs exposes the hidden --checkers flag for every copy, mirror, and move route, but only crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/local.rs consumes it. Every wire-carrier diff explicitly passes no checker pool at crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:5106, and the remote support gates do not reject a nonzero value. Consequently a diagnostic remote invocation accepts --checkers N while running unchanged, which can invalidate performance measurements; remote routes should reject the flag until they implement it.
